title: A fully supported local intricacy maximum among stationary binary one-step Markov laws
record_title: A fully supported local information maximum on the full two-shift
statement: Let $(X,T)$ be the full two-shift, let $\alpha$ be the partition used to define information, and consider the space of one-step Markov measures on $X$. title: A Latin maximum-agreement strategy that is not optimal for the finite field objective
record_title: Latin-strategy characterization conjecture for the symmetric group
statement:
Let $\mathbb{S}_n$ be the symmetric group on $n$ elements. A **Latin strategy** is obtained by choosing an $n\times n$ Latin square $S$; Alice's message identifies a row of $S$ that agrees with the input permutation at the maximum possible number of positions. An optimal strategy is one attaining the maximum success probability.

**Latin-strategy characterization conjecture.** Optimal strategies are exactly Latin strategies.

This conjecture proposes a complete characterization of optimal strategies, extending the explicitly described shift strategies. The paper states it as an open question and does not prove the characterization.
source: Artur Czumaj, George Kontogeorgiou and Mike Paterson, “Haystack Hunting Hints and Locker Room Communication”, arXiv:2008.11448 (2021).

title: A seven-vertex counterexample to the minimum-degree bound for Staller fast Maker-Breaker domination
record_title: Improved upper bounds for Staller–Maker–Breaker domination numbers
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with minimum degree $\delta(G)$. The S-game and D-game parameters are denoted by $\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)$ and $\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)$, respectively.

**Improved SMBD-number bounds.**

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{(i) If }\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)<\infty,\text{ then }\gamma_{\rm SMB}'(G)\le \left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil-\delta(G)+1;\\
&\text{(ii) If }\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)<\infty,\text{ then }\gamma_{\rm SMB}(G)\le \left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor-\delta(G)+1.
\end{aligned}
$$

These bounds would improve the known sharp general upper bounds when the minimum degree is at least two; the authors note that sharp examples under this degree condition are not known.
source: Csilla Bujtás and Pakanun Dokyeesun, “Fast winning strategies for Staller in the Maker-Breaker domination game”, arXiv:2206.12812 (2022).

title: No four-label edge coloring of K5 distinguishes all triangles by color sets
record_title: The set-palette conjecture for complete graphs
statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices. In a general edge-coloring of $K_n$, let $\tau_s(n)$ denote the minimum number of colors needed so that all triangles have distinct color palettes when a palette is viewed as the set of colors appearing on its three edges. **Set-palette conjecture.** For $n\geq4$,

$$
\tau_s(n)=n-1.
$$

The source notes the inequality $\tau_m(n)\leq\tau_s(n)\leq\tau'(n)$ and states that this conjecture would imply the preceding multiset-palette conjecture. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
source: Monika Pilsniak and Mariusz Wozniak, “A note on edge colorings distinguishing all triangles in a graph”, arXiv:2407.19050 (2024).
scope: Every map E(K5)->Fin 4 has two distinct triangles with equal edge-color sets; refutes Pilsniak-Wozniak arXiv:2407.19050v1 Conjecture 5 (tau_s(n)=n-1 for all n>=4) at n=5. Multiset Conjecture 4 untouched.

title: The prime field is not a maximal clique in GP(5^8,3): a counterexample to Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture
record_title: Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture for generalized Paley graphs
statement: Let $d>1$ be an integer. Let $q \equiv 1 \pmod {2d}$ be a power of a prime $p$, and let $r$ be the largest integer such that $d \mid \frac{q-1}{p^r-1}$. The subfield $\mathbb{F}_{p^r}$ is a clique in the generalized Paley graph $GP(q,d)=\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{F}_q^+;(\mathbb{F}_q^*)^d)$. **Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture.** The subfield $\mathbb{F}_{p^r}$ forms a maximal clique in $GP(q,d)$. This conjecture asserts that the largest subfield producing a subfield clique cannot be extended to a larger clique. The paper resolves it in a stronger form under a sufficient-size hypothesis, while the unrestricted statement is the conjecture being addressed.
source: Chi Hoi Yip, “Maximality of subfields as cliques in Cayley graphs over finite fields”, arXiv:2209.00864 (2022).
scope: For q=5^8, d=3 (largest admissible r=1), in every field of order 5^8 the prime field F_5 is a clique of GP(5^8,3) but not maximal (x=2θ+4θ^2+θ^3, f(θ)=0, f=X^8+X^7+2X^6+2). Refutes the unrestricted conjecture; ALCO Theorem 1.2 (q>(n-1)^2) untouched.

title: Complete bipartite graphs maximise sigma_t-irregularity among connected triangle-free graphs
record_title: Maximum sigma_t-irregularity conjecture for connected triangle-free graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a connected triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices. Write $sigma_t(G)$ for its $sigma_t$-irregularity. Among such graphs, the extremal complete bipartite graphs are conjectured to have maximum $sigma_t(G)$.

**Triangle-free extremal conjecture.** Among connected triangle-free graphs on $n$ vertices, the extremal complete bipartite graphs have the maximum $sigma_t(G)$-irregularity.

The paper proves the corresponding extremal result among complete bipartite graphs and proposes this conjecture as the extension to all connected triangle-free graphs; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
source: Slobodan Filipovski, Darko Dimitrov, Martin Knor and Riste Škrekovski, “Some results on σ_t-irregularity”, arXiv:2411.04881 (2024).

title: A six-point ordinal space with the majorization property that does not embed in the real line
record_title: The majorization characterization conjecture for ordinal spaces embeddable in the line
statement:
Let $(X,\delta)$ be an ordinal space with $|X|=n\in\mathbb N^+$, and let $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$ be an enumeration of its points satisfying the majorization property. Write $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^1$ for embeddability of $X$ in the real line. **Majorization characterization conjecture.** If such an enumeration exists, then

$$
X\hookrightarrow\mathbb R^1.
$$

The paper proves that line embeddability implies the existence of an enumeration with the majorization property and states sufficiency for $n\leqslant4$, while explicitly saying that it cannot determine whether sufficiency holds for $n>5$; the general assertion is therefore open.
source: Karsten Keller and Evgeniy Petrov, “Ordinal spaces”, arXiv:2412.17391 (2024).

title: A 34-vertex maximal rigid diameter-5 subset of the eight-dimensional Hamming cube
record_title: Largest rigid facet conjecture for Vietoris–Rips complexes of hypercubes
statement:
Let $Q_n=\\{\pm1\\}^n$ be the Hamming cube with Hamming distance. A subset is **maximally diameter-$r$** if its diameter is $r$ and adjoining any point outside it produces diameter greater than $r$; it is **rigid** if every point has a point at distance equal to the diameter. Let $b'(n;r)$ be the size of the largest maximally diameter-$r$, rigid subset of $Q_n$, equivalently the largest such rigid facet in $\operatorname{\mathcal{VR}}(Q_n;r)$. **Largest rigid facet conjecture.**

$$
b'(n;r)=2^r
$$

whenever $n\geq r$. The subcube $Q_r\times\\{\mathbf 1_{n-r}\\}$ supplies an extremal candidate of size $2^r$, but the conjectured upper bound is not proved in the source.
source: Joseph Briggs, Ziqin Feng and Chris Wells, “Facets in the Vietoris–Rips complexes of hypercubes”, arXiv:2408.01288 (2024).
scope: Explicit 34-point subset of signed Q_8 with diameter exactly 5, inclusion-maximal subject to diameter <= 5, and a diameter partner at every point; hence b'(8;5) >= 34 > 32, refuting Briggs-Feng-Wells Conjecture 1 (b'(n;r)=2^r for n>=r).

title: A quarter-table change from a group to a classical Moufang loop of order 16
record_title: The distance bound for loops with nonequivalent associator
statement:
Let $L=(G,\circ)$ and $M=(G,*)$ be Moufang loops on the same set $G$ of order $n$, and define their distance by

$$
d(\circ,*)=\left|\{(a,b)\in G\times G: a\circ b\ne a*b\}\right|.
$$
 Suppose that $L$ and $M$ have nonequivalent associators. **Distance-bound conjecture.** Their distance satisfies

$$
d(\circ,*)\ge 3n^2/8.
$$
 This conjecture asks for the minimum distance between Moufang loops with nonequivalent associator; the source gives no evidence of a proof or disproof.
source: Aleš Drápal and Petr Vojtěchovský, “Moufang loops that share associator and three quarters of their multiplication tables”, arXiv:math/0701710 (2007).

title: Exact super edge-magic total strength of a seven-cycle with four leaves at one vertex
record_title: Conjecture on the super edge-magic total strength of odd-cycle unicyclic graphs
statement:
Let $G(n;k_{1},\dots,k_{n})$ be the super edge-magic total unicyclic $(p,q)$-graph consisting of an odd cycle

$$
C_n=\{a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n\}
$$

and $k_i$ pendant vertices adjacent to each $a_i$, for $1\leq i\leq n$. Here $s m(G)$ denotes the super edge-magic total strength of $G$. **Super edge-magic total strength conjecture.**

$$
s m(G(n;k_{1},\dots,k_{n}))=2q+\frac{n+3}{2}.
$$

The claim extends the known exact value for the uniform family $k_i=k$, while the paper presents computations for certain graphs in this broader family as supporting evidence; its general validity remains open.
source: Nayana Shibu Deepthi, “Super edge-magic total strength of some unicyclic graphs”, arXiv:2212.05329 (2022).

title: An explicit non-collapsing facet of the 4 x 4 x 5 marginal cone
record_title: The collapsing conjecture for facets of hierarchical model polytopes
statement:
Let $p\leq q\leq r$ be positive integers, and let $P_\Delta^{p,q,r}$ denote the polytope associated with the hierarchical model in the paper. A facet is **obtained by collapsing** if it arises from a facet of a smaller table through the paper's collapsing operation.

**Collapsing conjecture.** Suppose that

$$
p \leq q \leq r.
$$

Then all facets of $P_\Delta^{p,q,r}$ are obtained by collapsing from facets of $P_\Delta^{p,q,q}$.

The conjecture is motivated by computational results summarized in the paper's table, although the authors also exhibit a non-collapsible facet of $P_\Delta^{4,4,4}$, showing that not every facet arises by collapsing to a binary table. The conjecture remains open in the supplied source.
source: Nicholas Eriksson, Stephen E. Fienberg, Alessandro Rinaldo and Seth Sullivant, “Polyhedral conditions for the nonexistence of the MLE for hierarchical log-linear models”, arXiv:math/0405044 (2004).

title: A wedge-complement domain with a nonstarlike Cassinian ball
record_title: Starlikeness conjecture for Cassinian balls in starlike domains
statement: Let $G\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a domain that is starlike with respect to $x\in G$, and let $B_{c_G}(x,r)$ denote the Cassinian ball of radius $r$. **Starlikeness conjecture.** For every $r>0$, the ball $B_{c_G}(x,r)$ is starlike with respect to $x$. title: All corrected odd-open and even-closed XOR-magic degrees at powers of two
record_title: Existence of regular open and closed XOR-magic graphs of power-of-two order
statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $d$ be a degree. An **open XOR-magic graph** and a **closed XOR-magic graph** are graphs admitting, respectively, an open or closed XOR-magic labeling. The graphs below are required to have order $2^n$.

For each degree

$$
d\in\{5,7,\ldots,2^n-7,2^n-5\},
$$

there exists a $d$-regular open XOR-magic graph of order $2^n$. For each degree

$$
d\in\{4,6,\ldots,2^n-6,2^n-4\},
$$

there exists a $d$-regular closed XOR-magic graph of order $2^n$.

**Existence conjecture.** For every permitted degree $d$ in the two displayed sets, the corresponding regular open or closed XOR-magic graph exists. This would complete the existence picture apart from the degrees excluded by the previously stated nonexistence result and extend the constructions known for order $16$ and order $8$ to every order that is a power of two.
source: Sylwia Cichacz, Hubert Grochowski and Rita Zuazua, “Open XOR-magic odd graphs and closed XOR-magic even graphs”, arXiv:2512.19278 (2025).
endpoints: XorMagic.corrected_all : ∀ n : ℕ, 4 ≤ n → CorrectedAt n; XorMagic.not_printed_each_ge_four : ∀ n : ℕ, 4 ≤ n → ¬ PrintedAt n (also printed_not_all, printed_not_positive)
scope: Cichacz-Grochowski-Zuazua Conjecture 25 (arXiv:2512.19278) as printed is false at every n>=4 because closed degree 2^n-4 is excluded by Proposition 24 (Batal); that correction is zero-credit. The intended conjecture (MathDB: 'apart from the degrees excluded by the previously stated nonexistence result') is proved in full: for every n>=4 there are connected simple open zero-XOR graphs on 2^n vertices of every odd degree 5..2^n-5 and closed ones of every even degree 4..2^n-6, which with Proposition 24 is the complete existence picture for the odd-open and even-closed classes.

title: A vertex of the asymmetric subtour elimination polytope on eight nodes that is adjacent to no tour
record_title: The neighborhood-tour conjecture for ASEP vertices
statement: Let $P_{\text{ASEP}}^{n}$ be the asymmetric subtour elimination polytope, let $\boldsymbol{x}$ be a vertex of this polytope, and let $\mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{x})$ denote its neighborhood in the vertex structure considered by the paper. title: An adverse non-Q graph from the cyclic Latin square of order six
record_title: Cardoso–Luz conjecture on adverse graphs
statement:
An **adverse graph** is a graph $H$ without isolated vertices such that $upsilon(H)$ and $lambda_{min}(H)$ are integers, and, for every vertex $i\in V(H)$,

$$
\upsilon(H-N_H(i))=\upsilon(H),\qquad \lambda_{min}(H-N_H(i))=\lambda_{min}(H).
$$

Here $upsilon(H)$ is the optimal value of the quadratic stability-number bound and $lambda_{min}(H)$ is the least eigenvalue of $H$. A graph is a **$\mathcal{Q}$-graph** when it belongs to the class $\mathcal{Q}$ defined in the paper.

**Cardoso–Luz conjecture.** All adverse graphs are $\mathcal{Q}$-graphs.

Computational tests with adverse graphs supported the conjecture, but it remains open. Its resolution would clarify the polynomial-time recognition of $\mathcal{Q}$-graphs.
source: Domingos M. Cardoso, “A survey on graphs with convex quadratic stability number”, arXiv:1811.05516 (2018).
endpoints: Adverse381433.refutation_of_source_statement : ¬ SourceConjecture (with edge hypothesis); Adverse381433.refutation : ¬ CardosoLuzConjecture; IndependentReview.refutes_stricter_source (non-complete variant, reviewer-authored)

This refutes Cardoso-Luz Conjecture 4.2 (survey arXiv:1811.05516, Optimization 69(1) 2020) that all adverse graphs are Q-graphs, also under the JCO 2016 'non complete' reading.

title: A clique with a five-edge tail reverses the hubs-biased Kirchhoff ordering
record_title: Estrada–Mugnolo's Kirchhoff-index ordering conjecture for hubs-biased resistance distances
statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. Write $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=1}}}(G)$ for the Kirchhoff index based on the hubs-repelling resistance distance, $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}}_{\alpha=0}(G)$ for the standard Kirchhoff index, and $\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=-1}}}(G)$ for the Kirchhoff index based on the hubs-attracting resistance distance.

**Kirchhoff-index ordering conjecture.** For $\alpha\in\{-1,1\}$,

$$
\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=1}}}(G)\geq\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}}_{\alpha=0}(G)\geq\mathcal{\mathcal{\mathscr{R}}_{\mathnormal{\alpha=-1}}}(G),
$$

with equality if and only if $G$ is regular.

The conjecture was formulated after computational experiments on more than 12,000 connected graphs with $5\leq n\leq 8$, and predicts that hubs-repelling navigation gives the largest Kirchhoff index while hubs-attracting navigation gives the smallest. Its general validity is left open in the source.
source: Ernesto Estrada and Delio Mugnolo, “Hubs-biased resistance distances on graphs and networks”, arXiv:2101.07103 (2021).
endpoints: KirchhoffReal.refuteSpec : ¬ LiteralConjecture GroupInverse spectralIndex (Lemma 4.6 spectral reading, primary substantive result); KirchhoffReal.refuteMP : ¬ LiteralConjecture Penrose pairIndex (literal (4.3) Moore-Penrose reading)

title: A parity-corrected potential proves the Elsholtz–Klahn–Lipnik four-term progression-free digit-set conjecture
record_title: The prime-modulus conjecture for progression-free digit sets
statement:
Let $p\geq 13$ be a prime with $p\equiv 1\bmod 4$, and let $n$ be an integer divisible by $(p+3)/2$. For a digit set $D\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_p$, write $S(D,n)$ for the set of vectors in $\mathbb{Z}_p^n$ in which every digit of $D$ occurs the same number of times. Define

$$
D=\left\{0,1,\ldots,\frac{p-1}{2},\frac{p+3}{2}\right\}.
$$

**Prime-modulus progression-free-set conjecture.** The set $S(D,n)$ does not contain any arithmetic progression of length $4$.

title: A cubic counterexample to edge-pattern convex domination
record_title: The edge-pattern convex-combination conjecture
statement:
Let $P$ be a $d$-regular edge-rooted pattern of depth $r$ and girth $2r+2$. For each edge-rooted pattern, let $\mathbf{e}(P)$ denote its constraint vector, and let $\mathcal{T}'_r(d)$ be the specified family of $d$-regular edge-rooted trees of depth $r$. The constraint $\mathbf{e}(P)$ is **weaker** than a convex combination of constraints from this family in the sense that there exist $T_1,\dots,T_m\in\mathcal{T}'_r(d)$ and $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_m\in[0,1]$ with

$$
\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1
$$

and, for every $\bm{\alpha}\in{\left(\mathbb{Q}^+\right)}^{r+1}$,

$$
\bm{\alpha}^{\!\top}\left(\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\mathbf{e}(T_i)\right)\ge 1\quad\implies\quad\bm{\alpha}^{\!\top}\mathbf{e}(P)\ge 1.
$$

This would explain why the bounds obtained from edge-rooted trees remain valid at girth $2r+2$, and would generalize the cases checked for $r=2$ and $d\in\{3,4\}$.
source: François Pirot and Jean-Sébastien Sereni, “Fractional chromatic number, maximum degree and girth”, arXiv:1904.05618 (2021).
scope: Pirot-Sereni (arXiv:1904.05618; SIAM J. Discrete Math. 35(4) (2021) 2815-2843) Conjecture 2, also Conjecture 1.5.1 of Pirot's 2019 thesis, is false at d = 3, r = 2. The 8-vertex edge-rooted pattern P (root edge 01; edges 01,02,03,15,17,34,46,56: a 6-cycle with two pendants) is 3-regular, of exact depth 2 and girth 6, with e(P) = (2/5,14/5,4/5). So no convex combination of tree constraints is weaker than e(P). The source's optimized bounds (Lemma 10) are unaffected.

\sum_{\substack{\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n\\min(\operatorname{type}(\pi))\geq k}}(-1)^{\operatorname{inv}(\pi)}\mathbf{x}_{\operatorname{RLMv}(\pi)}\mathbf{y}_{\operatorname{EXCv}(\pi)}
$$

title: GM strategies are not a Nash equilibrium in l-player exact slow NIM(n, n-1) for n, l >= 3: a refutation of Gurvich-Naumova Conjecture 1 (arXiv:2311.03257)
record_title: The GM-rule Nash equilibrium conjecture for exact slow NIM
statement: Consider the exact slow game NIM$(n,n-1)$ for $\ell$ players: a position is a non-negative $n$-vector, players move cyclically, and on each move a player keeps one entry unchanged and decreases each of the other $n-1$ positive entries by $1$. A position with at least two non-positive entries is terminal; the player whose turn it is loses, and the other $\ell-1$ players share the payoff $\frac{C-L(P)}{\ell-1}$, where $L(P)$ is the play length and $C$ exceeds the length of every play from the initial position. The GM-rule specifies a strategy for each player, including the move that keeps the largest entry when no entry is a multiple of $\ell$. **GM-rule Nash equilibrium conjecture.** The set of $\ell$ GM-strategies forms a uniform Nash equilibrium. The claim concerns the strategic behavior induced by the GM-rule in the multiplayer exact slow NIM game; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or disproved.

title: An Euler tour of the full permutation overlap graph that no cyclic word realizes: a refutation of Hurlbert's ordering conjecture for universal cycles of permutations
record_title: Hurlbert's ordering conjecture for universal cycles of permutations
statement: Let $S_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]$, and let $\mathcal{O}(n)$ be the clustered graph of overlapping $n$-permutations: its edges are the permutations in $S_n$, and consecutive permutations overlap in their last and first $n-1$ entries up to reduction. **Hurlbert's ordering conjecture.** Given any Euler tour of the clustered graph of overlapping permutations (that is, an ordering of $S_n$ such that each consecutive pair of permutations overlaps), there is a universal cycle for permutations that covers $S_n$ in the same order. title: A symmetric kernel certificate for Hetyei's second-kind interval transform: a refutation of the kernel conjecture (Discrete Comput. Geom. 2024, Conjecture 39)

title: A rank-four nine-element counterexample to Lason common-basis conjecture

statement:

title: The balanced-graph conjecture for flat graphs is false
record_title: Balanced-graph conjecture for flat graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a flat graph, and let $c_i(G)$ denote the number of $i$-cliques in $G$. Define

$$
D_{clique}(G)=\left|\sum_{i:\ i\ \mathrm{is\ odd}}c_i(G)-\sum_{i:\ i\ \mathrm{is\ even}}c_i(G)\right|.
$$

Call $G$ **balanced** when $D_{clique}(G)\leq 1$.

title: The Polynexus ordered-pair formula for the contiguous-diagonal rook submonoid
record_title: The Polynexus formula for nonzero products in the rook monoid
statement:
Let $M_n$ be the monoid of rook diagrams and let $\mathbf{0}$ denote its zero element. Let $\psi(n)$ be the number of nonzero products arising from $M_n\setminus\{\mathbf{0}\}$.

**Polynexus conjecture.** For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\psi(n)$ equals the $(n+1)$th Polynexus number of order $7$, namely

$$
\psi(n)=\frac{(n+1)^7-n^7-(n+1)^3+n^3}{120}.
$$

The formula was suggested by numerical evaluation of the sextuple sum defining $\psi(n)$ and comparison with the Polynexus numbers. An analytic evaluation of that sum was not available in the source, so the conjecture remains open here.
source: George Fikioris and Giannis Fikioris, “A subsemigroup of the rook monoid”, arXiv:2111.01863 (2022).

title: Extremal trees for the biharmonic index

title: The list color function threshold of K_{2,l}

title: The local weak limit of uniform random fullerenes

title: The Q-index of K_{t,s+1}-free graphs
record_title: The Q-index extremal conjecture for $K_{t,s+1}$-free graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, with adjacency matrix $A$ and diagonal degree matrix $D$. Its signless Laplacian is $Q(G)=A+D$, and its $Q$-index $q(G)$ is the largest eigenvalue of $Q(G)$. A graph is **$K_{t,s+1}$-free** if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to the complete bipartite graph $K_{t,s+1}$. Let $s\geq t-1\geq1$, and let $n$ be sufficiently large. **The Q-index extremal conjecture.** If $G$ is a $K_{t,s+1}$-free graph of order $n$, then

$$
q(G)\leq\frac{n}{2}+s+t-2+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\left(n-2+2s\right)^2-8s\left(n-2\right)+4\left(t-1\right)\left(n-t+1\right)}.
$$

Equality holds if and only if $G$ is the join of $K_{t-1}$ and an $s$-regular graph of order $n-t+1$. The conjecture is proposed as a spectral counterpart to extremal problems for $K_{s,t}$-free graphs; the authors state that they expect Problem C to be resolved completely in the next few years, but the asserted bound and equality characterization remain unproved here.
source: Maria Aguieiras A. de Freitas, Vladimir Nikiforov and Laura Patuzzi, “Maxima of the Q-index: graphs with no K_s,t”, arXiv:1507.00625 (2015).

title: Harada partition-statistic inequality
record_title: Conjecture on the partition-function bound in Harada's conjecture
statement:

$$

This inequality arises from the contribution of degree-one polynomials to the valuation polynomial associated with $h(\operatorname{GL}_n(k))$. Its validity would support the expected positivity behind the integrality of the Harada invariant in higher rank, but the conjecture is left open in the supplied text.

title: Counterexample to the characteristic-imset sink-edge conjecture
record_title: The local reversal edge conjecture for characteristic imset polytopes
statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a directed acyclic graph with skeleton $G$, and let $i$ be a vertex. Define $\mathcal{G}_{\downarrow i}$ by orienting every edge between $i$ and a neighbor toward $i$, while leaving all other edges as in $\mathcal{G}$. $$
\operatorname{conv}\left(c_\mathcal{G},c_{\mathcal{G}_{\downarrow i}}\right)
$$

is an edge of $\CIM_G$. A linear bound on the diameter of $\CIM_G$ would follow from this conjecture; the source establishes quadratic bounds in general and linear bounds for trees and for the whole polytope, but does not resolve the conjecture for arbitrary skeletons.

title: All-minimizer asymptotic balance for the sum-Balaban index of dumbbells
record_title: Asymptotic dumbbell conjecture for the minimum sum-Balaban index
statement:
Let $D_{a,b,a'}$ be a dumbbell graph on $n$ vertices, with clique sizes $a$ and $a'$ and connecting path size $b$, so that $a+b+a'=n$. Let

$$
c=\sqrt[4]{\sqrt 2\log\big(1+\sqrt 2\big)}.

**Asymptotic dumbbell conjecture.** Among all dumbbell graphs $D_{a,b,a'}$ on $n$ vertices, the minimum is achieved for one with

$$
a=c\sqrt n+o(\sqrt n),\qquad a'=c\sqrt n+o(\sqrt n),\qquad b=n-o(n).
$$

This conjecture gives the predicted asymptotic shape of an optimal dumbbell graph: the two cliques have equal asymptotic size, while the path contains almost all vertices. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

title: Uniform frustrated-cycle stability below a star threshold
record_title: Generalisation of the frustrated-triangle extremal conjecture to frustrated cycles
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\overline{G}$ denote its complement, and for $k\geq 3$ let $f_k(G)$ be the number of frustrated $k$-cycles, where a cyclic ordering $v_1v_2\dots v_k$ is frustrated when an odd number of its consecutive cycle edges belongs to $G$. For integers $t\geq 0$, let a $(t+1)$-star on $n$ vertices be the graph consisting of a star with $t+1$ leaves together with the remaining isolated vertices. **Frustrated-cycle generalisation conjecture.** For every $k\geq 3$, $t\geq 0$, and all sufficiently large $n$, if

$$
f_k(G)<f_k\big((t+1)\text{-star on }n\text{ vertices}\big),
$$

then either $G$ or $\overline{G}$ can be obtained from a complete bipartite graph by flipping at most $t$ edges or non-edges. This proposes an extension of the paper's structural result for frustrated triangles to frustrated cycles; its resolution is not given in the source.

title: Uniform-matroid weighted finite multiplier theorem
record_title: The $d$-sequence conjecture for coefficients of uniform-matroid $Z$-polynomials
statement:
For integers $m$ and $d$, and $0\leq i\leq d$, define

$$
b_m(d,i)=\sum_{h=0}^{m-1}\frac{i(h-m+1)+m}{(h+1)m}\binom{i-1+h}{h}\binom{d-i+h}{h}.

The conjecture is proposed as the analogue of the corresponding assertion for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials and would support real-rootedness results for uniform-matroid $Z$-polynomials; its general status remains open.

title: Universal symmetries of rooted directed compass boards
record_title: Symmetry classification conjecture for board isomorphisms
statement:
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be the set of eight arrow directions, let $\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times n}(\mathcal{D})$ be the set of boards, and let $\operatorname{Sym}(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times n}(\mathcal{D}))$ be the group of coordinate permutations and direction permutations that preserve graph isomorphism for every board. Let $R$ be reflection through the main diagonal, defined by $R(A)_{ij}=(a_{ji})^T$. **Symmetry classification conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{Sym}(\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times n}(\mathcal{D}))=\{Id,R\}.
$$

The reflection $R$ is known to belong to this symmetry group, so the assertion is that it is the only nontrivial universal symmetry of boards. The source provides no resolution of this classification question.
source: Ary Shaviv, “Board games, random boards and long boards”, arXiv:2110.05416 (2021).

title: The sparsity conjecture for minimally AP-irreducible sign patterns
record_title: The sparsity conjecture for minimally AP-irreducible sign pattern matrices
statement:
Let $A$ be a minimally AP-irreducible sign pattern matrix of order $n$ whose diagonal entries are all zero. A sign pattern matrix $A$ is **minimally AP-irreducible** if it is AP-irreducible and deleting any nonzero entry destroys AP-irreducibility. **Sparsity conjecture.** The matrix $A$ has at most $2n-2$ nonzero entries.

The paper establishes this bound under the additional hypothesis that $A[\alpha,\beta]$ contains no $+$ for any two distinct irreducible components $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of $A_+$. The conjecture asks whether the same bound holds without that additional hypothesis; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
source: Sunil Das, “Sign patterns that allow algebraic positivity”, arXiv:2112.00442 (2022).

title: Prescribed-endpoint Hamiltonian paths in Cartesian products of directed cycles
record_title: Hamiltonian-path distance congruence conjecture for Cartesian products of directed cycles
statement:
Let $X$ be the Cartesian product of $k$ directed cycles of lengths $m_1,m_2,\ldots,m_k$, where $k\geq 3$ and each $m_i\geq 2$. For vertices $u$ and $v$ of $X$, let $d_X(u,v)$ denote the length of a shortest directed path from $u$ to $v$. **Hamiltonian-path distance congruence conjecture.** There is a Hamiltonian path from $u$ to $v$ if and only if

$$
d_X(u,v)\equiv -1\pmod{\gcd(m_1,m_2,\ldots,m_k)}.
$$
 This generalizes the coprime-length case, in which the congruence condition is automatic, and remains open according to the supplied source.
source: David Austin, Heather Gavlas and Dave Witte, “Hamiltonian Paths in Cartesian Powers of Directed Cycles”, arXiv:math/0110073 (2001).

title: Caterpillar and balanced species tree growth-factor conjecture
record_title: Caterpillar and balanced species tree growth-factor conjecture
statement:
Let $k$ be fixed and let $n$ be sufficiently large. An **unranked species tree** is a species tree considered up to isomorphism, and a **caterpillar tree** and a **balanced species tree** are, respectively, the extreme unbalanced and balanced species-tree shapes of size $k$. The ${\mathbb{D}\mathbb{L}}$-histories are histories in the duplication-loss model.

**Caterpillar and balanced species tree conjecture.** For a given $k$ and sufficiently large $n$, the unranked species tree of size $k$ having the largest number of ${\mathbb{D}\mathbb{L}}$-histories of size $n$ is the caterpillar tree. Moreover, the exponential growth factor of the number of histories for a caterpillar of size $k$ grows superlinearly as a function of $k$. Species trees having the smallest number of ${\mathbb{D}\mathbb{L}}$-histories are balanced species trees of size $k$, and the exponential growth factor of the number of histories for a balanced tree of size $k$ grows linearly as a function of $k$.

This conjecture characterizes the species-tree shapes that produce the largest and smallest numbers of duplication-loss histories for fixed species-tree size. The source presents these growth assertions as conclusions suggested by experiments; no proof or resolution is given.
source: Cedric Chauve, Yann Ponty and Michael Wallner, “Counting and sampling gene family evolutionary histories in the duplication-loss and duplication-loss-transfer models”, arXiv:1905.04971 (2019).

title: Existence conjecture for D-optimal rhombic designs
record_title: Existence conjecture for D-optimal rhombic designs
statement:
Let $K$ be the dimension, let $D$ be the covariance matrix of the random coefficients, and let $(d_0,d_1,d_2)^T\in\mathcal{C}_K$ denote its parameter vector. A **rhombic design** is an invariant design from the class studied for the multiple linear regression model on the hypercube, and a design is **$D$-optimal** if it maximizes the determinant of its information matrix under covariance matrix $D$. **Existence conjecture.** For even $K$, there is a $D$-optimal rhombic design for all

$$
(d_0,d_1,d_2)^T\in\mathcal{C}_K.
$$

For odd $K$, there is a $D$-optimal rhombic design for all

$$
(d_0,d_1,d_2)^T\in\mathcal{C}_K\quad\text{with}\quad d_2\leq\frac{d_1}{2}.
$$

The conjecture records the observed existence pattern for $D$-optimal rhombic designs: existence was found for all parameter values in even dimensions, whereas in odd dimensions it was established only in the stated region. Whether such designs exist for all remaining parameter values when $K$ is odd is left open.
source: Ulrike Graßhoff, Heinz Holling, Frank Röttger and Rainer Schwabe, “Optimality regions for designs in multiple linear regression models with correlated random coefficients”, arXiv:1911.05538 (2019).

title: Uniform residue-class bias for part occurrences in bounded-multiplicity partitions
record_title: Congruence-class bias conjecture for parts in k-regular partitions
statement:
For $k$-regular partitions, let $D_k(r,t;n)$ denote the number of occurrences of parts congruent to $r$ modulo $t$ among the partitions of $n$. Here $t\geq 6$, $1\leq r<s\leq t$, and $k\geq 3$.

**Congruence-class bias conjecture.** For $n\geq 1$,

$$
D_k(r,t;n) \geq D_k(s,t;n).
$$

Moreover, for $k\geq 2$, if

$$
n>\max\{t+3,16\},
$$

then

$$
D_k(r,t;n)>D_k(s,t;n).
$$

The conjecture formalizes the observed bias toward smaller parts and extends the finite computational verification to all $t\geq 6$ and all admissible congruence classes. The preceding theorem establishes related bounds for $2\leq k,t\leq 10$, while the asserted ranges beyond those finite checks remain open.
source: Faye Jackson and Misheel Otgonbayar, “Biases among Congruence Classes for Parts in k-regular Partitions”, arXiv:2207.04352 (2022).

title: Nian–Tsujie–Uchiumi–Yoshinaga limit conjecture for q-deformed graphic arrangements
record_title: Nian–Tsujie–Uchiumi–Yoshinaga limit conjecture for q-deformed graphic arrangements
statement:

$$
\lim_{q\to 1}\frac{\chi(\mathcal{A}_G^q,q^s)}{(q-1)^\ell}=\chi(G,s).
$$

title: The finite-cycle character-value coincidence conjecture for symmetric groups
record_title: The finite-cycle character-value coincidence conjecture for symmetric groups
statement:
Let $X$ be a finite set of permutations, and let $k\geq 1$ be an integer. For a permutation $g\in S_n$, its cycle type is the multiset of lengths of its cycles.

The conjecture asks for arbitrarily large collections of distinct irreducible characters that cannot be distinguished by their values on any prescribed finite set of cycle types. The source contrasts it with an adaptive procedure for determining characters from values and gives computational examples, but leaves the conjecture open.
source: David A. Craven, “On the irreducible character degrees of symmetric groups and their multiplicities”, arXiv:2410.01726 (2025).

title: Finiteness conjecture for connected graphs with odd metamour period
record_title: Finiteness conjecture for connected graphs with odd metamour period
statement:
A graph's **metamour period** is the least positive integer $k$ for which its iterated metamour graph returns to the original graph, under the metamour operation used in the paper. Let $k$ range over the positive odd integers.

**Finiteness conjecture.** For each odd $k\in \mathbb{Z}^+$, there exist only finitely many connected graphs with metamour period $k$.

The paper has already classified the connected graphs with metamour period $3$: they are $C_7$ and $C_9$. The conjecture predicts analogous finiteness for every odd period, and the classification of such graphs remains open in general.
source: William Q. Erickson, Daniel Herden, Jonathan Meddaugh, Mark R. Sepanski, Mitchell Minyard and Kyle Rosengartner, “Limits and Periodicity of Metamour 2-Distance Graphs”, arXiv:2409.02306 (2024).
scope: SUBSTANTIVE_BOUNDED: explicit order bound at each odd metamour period via a temporal-word triangle obstruction and Ramsey degree bound; no complete bridge in inspected bodies.
limits: FAU abstract body, Leonor thesis and several primary bodies unread.

title: Failure of the matroid matching property in odd-dimensional rigidity matroids
record_title: Failure of the matroid matching property in odd-dimensional rigidity matroids
statement: For integers $k\geq 2$ and sufficiently large $n$, consider the rigidity matroid ${\mathcal R}_{2k+1}(K_n)$ of the complete graph $K_n$ in dimension $2k+1$. **The matroid matching conjecture.** The matroid ${\mathcal R}_{2k+1}(K_n)$ does not have the matroid matching property for all $k\geq 2$ and sufficiently large $n$. The preceding proof establishes the corresponding even-dimensional result, while the odd-dimensional case is suspected to fail in this way for dimensions at least five and large complete graphs.
source: John Hewetson, Bill Jackson, Anthony Nixon and Ben Smith, “k-fold circuits and coning in rigidity matroids”, arXiv:2508.18838 (2026).
endpoints: literal endpoint per CROSSWALK.md (independent extracted replay PASS, 41 modules)
scope: MODEST_BOUNDED (close call): explicit pair family in odd dimension d>=5 with maximum matching h-2 against Dress-Lovasz minimum h-1; a reviewer derived an unpublished alternate coning route, which weakens the significance but is not prior art.
limits: User may overrule. Dress-Lovasz Springer body unread.

title: Cell-count conjecture for face Schubert arrangements of polytopes
record_title: Cell-count conjecture for face Schubert arrangements of polytopes
statement: Let $P\subseteq \mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ be a full-dimensional polytope, and let $P^{[k]}$ denote its $k$-stabbing set. Consider the $k$-face Schubert arrangement of $P$ inside $P^{[k]}$, and the sign vectors determined by its defining equations for $V\in P^{[k]}\setminus \mathcal{H}_P^k$. **Cell-count conjecture.** The number of cells in this arrangement is equal to the number of sign vectors realized by such spaces $V$. This would show that, for Schubert arrangements arising from polytopes, cells are uniquely determined by their realized sign vectors; the claim is presented as an expectation, and no resolution is supplied in the source.
source: Sebastian Seemann and Francesca Zaffalon, “How to stab a polytope”, arXiv:2412.00551 (2024).
scope: SUBSTANTIVE_BOUNDED: eight-vertex rational polytope with two stabbing lines sharing a strict sign vector in different components; convex realization not in inspected prior. Component finiteness is ordinary, the count inequality is kernel-checked.
limits: Pavlov-Ranestad journal final unread.

title: Lattice-realization conjecture for preorder lattice-point posets
record_title: Lattice-realization conjecture for preorder lattice-point posets
statement:
Let $\tau$ be a preorder of size $n$, let $P_\tau$ be its lattice-point poset, let $M_{P_\tau}(x,y)$ be its $M$-triangle, and let $\overline{M}_{P_\tau}$ be the transmutation defined by

$$
\overline f(x,y)=f\left(\frac{1-y}{1-xy},1-xy\right).
$$

**Lattice-realization conjecture.** There exists a finite graded lattice $L_\tau$ of rank $n$ such that

$$
\mathcal Z(P_\tau,t)=\mathcal Z(L_\tau,t),\qquad \overline M_{P_\tau}(x,y)=M_{L_\tau}(x,y).
$$

In particular, the rank-generating polynomial of $L_\tau$ equals $h(\tau,t)$. The conjecture extends the arbor setting; the source gives examples for chain preorders but no general resolution.
source: Frédéric Chapoton and Christos A. Athanasiadis, “Polytopes and posets associated to preorders”, arXiv:2605.26916 (2026).
scope: SUBSTANTIVE_MODEST: Conjecture 8.1 fails at the three-element corolla by a cover-incidence double count (13 required, at most 10 possible); contradicts the computational expectation in Chapoton section 9.
limits: All-corolla extension is ordinary only; Lean covers t3.

title: Treewidth-connectivity partition conjecture for graphs
record_title: Treewidth-connectivity partition conjecture for graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $k$ be an integer such that $G$ has treewidth at most $k$ and connectivity at least $k$. A vertex set inducing a graph of treewidth at most $k-1$ and connectivity at least $k-1$ is denoted by $\mathcal{T}$, and an independent set is denoted by $\mathcal{I}$. **Treewidth-connectivity partition conjecture.** The vertices of $G$ can be partitioned into an induced graph $\mathcal{T}$ of treewidth at most $k-1$ and connectivity at least $k-1$, and an independent set $\mathcal{I}$. This is proposed as a generalization of a theorem for graphs of treewidth at most $2$; the source leaves it as a belief rather than an established result.
source: Stijn Cambie, François Dross, Kolja Knauer, Hoang La and Petru Valicov, “Partitions of planar (oriented) graphs into a connected acyclic and an independent set”, arXiv:2412.11774 (2025).
scope: SUBSTANTIVE_BOUNDED: 16-vertex 34-edge graph of treewidth 3 and connectivity 3 with no admissible partition; extension to all k>=3 is ordinary only.
limits: EJC final scope unread.

title: Dickenstein–Nill Cayley decomposition conjecture for lattice polytopes
record_title: Dickenstein–Nill Cayley decomposition conjecture for lattice polytopes
statement:
Let $P$ be an $n$-dimensional lattice polytope, and let $cmu(P)$ denote its $cmathbb{Q}$-codegree. A **Cayley sum** is a polytope constructed by placing polytopes along the vertices of a standard simplex and taking their convex hull.

**Dickenstein–Nill's Cayley decomposition conjecture.** If

$$
\mu(P) > \frac{n+1}{2},
$$

then $P$ decomposes as a Cayley sum of lattice polytopes of dimension at most

$$
\left\lfloor 2(n+1-\mu(P)) \right\rfloor.
$$

The stronger conjecture by Dickenstein and Nill was disproved by Higashitani; the weaker version recorded here remains open. A slightly weaker statement, with the hypothesis $\mu(P) \geq \frac{n+2}{2}$, is known.
source: Sofía Garzón Mora and Christian Haase, “Fine Polyhedral Adjunction Theory”, arXiv:2302.04074 (2023).
scope: MODEST_BOUNDED (close call): direct heavy-slack projection proof of the Q-codegree Cayley decomposition conjecture, independent of DRHNP Theorem 3.4; the strongest objection is that Theorem 3.4 leaves only the even-dimensional width-one case, which is elementary.
limits: User may overrule. Garzon Mora FU Berlin dissertation unread; withdraw if it proves the conjecture.

title: The square power partition function inequality conjecture
record_title: The square power partition function inequality conjecture
statement:
Let $p^k(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ into perfect $k$-th powers. In particular, $p^2(n)$ is the square power partition function, and let $a,b$ be positive integers.

**Square power partition function inequality conjecture.** The inequality

$$
p^2(a)p^2(b)\geq p^2(a+b)
$$

has equality and failure exactly in the instances listed in the source's table: equality for $a=1$, $b=1,2,4,5,6,9,10,13,14,18,22$; $a=2$, $b=4,5,9,13$; $a=3$, $b=4$; $a=4$, $b=5,6,7$; $a=5$, $b=5,6,8,11,15$; $a=6$, $b=8,10,12,14$; and $a=7$, $b=8,9,12,13,19$, with the listed complementary instances of failure.

The claim refines the eventual multiplicative inequality for restricted partition functions by identifying its exceptional small-index behavior. The source gives no resolution beyond presenting these instances as a conjectural pattern.
source: Arindam Roy, “Log-concavity And The Multiplicative Properties of Restricted Partition Functions”, arXiv:2404.03153 (2025).
scope: SUBSTANTIVE_BOUNDED: exact global sign table for p2(a)p2(b) vs p2(a+b) (33 equalities, 10 failures with m>=4, strict success for m>=8); no inspected source proves an effective global cutoff.
limits: Springer final 10.1007/s00026-026-00847-5 unread.

title: The three-component-intersection extremal conjecture for odd n
record_title: The three-component-intersection extremal conjecture for odd n
statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ with $n$ odd, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of graphs on $[n]$.

**Three-component-intersection conjecture.** If the intersection of any two graphs in $\mathcal{F}$ has at most three components, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq \frac{(n+3)^2}{8}\frac{1}{2^n}\cdot 2^{\binom{n}{2}}.
$$

For more than two components, the authors report that fixed-Hamilton-cycle constructions no longer appear optimal. For three components they suspect the bound is attained by a construction based on two half-sized cycles meeting at a point, although the displayed conjecture is the stated quantitative claim.
source: Imre Leader, Žarko Ranđelović and Ta Sheng Tan, “A Note on Hamiltonian-Intersecting Families of Graphs”, arXiv:2309.00757 (2023).
scope: For every h >= 1, on n = 6h-1 labelled vertices there is a family of (1+6h+12h^2)*2^(C(n,2)-6h) graphs whose pairwise intersections all have at most three components, exceeding the conjectured bound ((n+3)^2/8)*2^(C(n,2)-n); the ratio tends to 4/3. The family consists of all graphs missing at most one edge from each of at most two of the three paths of a spanning theta graph. At n = 5 it has 304 graphs against a bound of 256. Lean proves the family for all h, failure above every order threshold, and the literal negation.
limits: The Discrete Mathematics journal version of the source is unread (publisher refuses automated access). The conjecture was restated unchanged in Randelovic 2025 Cambridge thesis.

title: Bóna's maximal-avoidance conjecture for Hertzsprung patterns
record_title: Bóna's maximal-avoidance conjecture for Hertzsprung patterns
statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}_k$ be the set of Hertzsprung patterns of length $k$, let $\tau\in\mathcal{S}_k$, and let $|\mathcal{S}_n(\tau)|$ denote the number of length-$n$ objects avoiding $\tau$. Write $\mathrm{id}_k$ for the identity pattern of length $k$. **Bóna's maximal-avoidance conjecture.** For every Hertzsprung pattern $\tau\in\mathcal{S}_k$ and every natural number $n$,

$$
|\mathcal{S}_n(\tau)|\leq |\mathcal{S}_n(\mathrm{id}_k)|.
$$

Bóna proved the inequality for non-self-overlapping patterns. The paper reports computational evidence suggesting that self-overlapping patterns also satisfy it, but gives no general proof.
source: Anders Claesson, “From Hertzsprung's problem to pattern-rewriting systems”, arXiv:2012.15309 (2021).
scope: For all k and n and every pattern tau in S_k, the number of permutations of [n] with no Hertzsprung occurrence of tau (consecutive positions, values order-isomorphic with a single shift) is at most the number with no Hertzsprung occurrence of the identity pattern of length k; the inequality is strict when k < n and tau is neither the identity nor its reverse. This is the maximal-avoidance conjecture of Bona as stated in Claesson Conjecture 3.13, including the self-overlapping patterns that the earlier argument did not cover. The proof compares first and second moments of occurrence counts.
limits: The 2008 Discrete Mathematics version of Bona's paper is unread (paywalled). One phrase about work associated with Claesson Conjecture 3.14 carries no citation.

title: Congruence conjectures for permanents of shifted difference matrices
record_title: Congruence conjectures for permanents of shifted difference matrices
statement:
For a positive integer $n$, let $[j-k+\delta_{jk}]_{1\leqslant j,k\leqslant n}$ denote the $n\times n$ matrix whose $(j,k)$ entry is $j-k+\delta_{jk}$, where $\delta_{jk}$ is the Kronecker delta, and let $\operatorname{per}(M)$ denote the permanent of a matrix $M$. **Congruence conjecture.** For any prime $p$,

$$
\operatorname{per}[j-k+\delta_{jk}]_{1\leqslant j,k\leqslant p-1}\equiv 3\pmod p.
$$

For any odd prime $p$,

$$
\operatorname{per}[j-k+\delta_{jk}]_{1\leqslant j,k\leqslant p}\equiv 1+4p\pmod {p^2}.
$$

These assertions are motivated by the preceding determinant evaluation in the paper; no resolution or external evidence concerning either congruence is supplied here.
source: Han Wang and Zhi-Wei Sun, “Evaluations of some Toeplitz-type determinants”, arXiv:2206.12317 (2023).
scope: Let B_n be the n by n integer matrix with entries j - k + delta_jk. For every prime p, per(B_{p-1}) is congruent to 3 modulo p, and for every odd prime p, per(B_p) is congruent to 1 + 4p modulo p^2. These are the two permanent congruences conjectured by Wang and Sun. The modulo p^2 congruence uses a new reflection lifting lemma and a telescoping factorial sum.
limits: Zhi-Wei Sun's 2021 Chinese-language book, cited by the source as motivation (Conjecture 11.23), is unread.

title: Linear-growth conjecture for Split Smallest and Combine Smallest games
record_title: Linear-growth conjecture for Split Smallest and Combine Smallest games
statement:
A Zeckendorf game starts from the Zeckendorf decomposition of $n$ and proceeds by legal combining and splitting moves; the **Split Smallest** and **Combine Smallest** games are deterministic strategies, and the number of moves is measured as the total number of moves in the resulting game.

**Linear-growth conjecture.** For Split Smallest, the number of moves grows linearly with $n$, with the asymptotic constant appearing numerically to be the square of the golden mean. For Combine Smallest games, the number of moves grows linearly with $n$, with the constant appearing numerically to be approximately $1.206$.

The paper presents these claims as data-supported conjectures for the two deterministic games whose behavior was not rigorously determined there.
source: Ruoci Li, Xiaonan Li, Steven J. Miller, Clayton Mizgerd, Chenyang Sun, Dong Xia and Zhyi Zhou, “Deterministic Zeckendorf Games”, arXiv:2006.16457 (2020).
scope: Source-bound resolution of the Combine Smallest half of Conjecture 1.4 for the deterministic Zeckendorf game started from n copies of F_1: the number of moves is CS(n) = c n + O(sqrt(n) log n) with c = 5/2 - phi + sum_{j>=2} 1/F_{2j} = 1.2064811686..., with an explicit error constant. The Split Smallest half (constant phi^2) is due to Cusenza et al. and is only attributed. The MathDB record states the start position as the Zeckendorf decomposition of n, which gives zero moves and makes the record trivially false as literally written; the result proves the statement with the source start position.
limits: Record defect: the MathDB start position differs from the source; accepted on the source statement by root judgment (held for a user ruling since 2026-11-09; user may overrule). Significance modest. The proved error term is far from sharp (numerically the error stays under about 20 up to n = 3*10^7).

title: Hook-partition formulae for Kadar–Yu Gram determinant polynomials
record_title: Hook-partition formulae for Kadar–Yu Gram determinant polynomials
statement:
Let $l$, $l'$, and $l”$ be integer parameters, and let $C^{(\lambda)}(\alpha)$ and $P_n^{(\lambda)}(\alpha)$ denote the factors in the Kadar–Yu Gram determinant formula for a partition $\lambda$. For the hook partitions $(l'+1,1)$ and the transpose $(l+1,1)^T$, the displayed expressions give their $C$-factors and Chebyshev expansions.

**Hook-partition formula conjecture.** Formulae for $C^{(l'+1,1)}(\alpha)$, $C^{(l+1,1)^T}(\alpha)$, $P^{(l”+1,1)}_{l”+4+k}(\alpha)$, and $P^{(l+1,1)^T}_{l+4+k}(\alpha)$ hold for all $l\geq 1$, $l'\geq 4$, and $l”\geq 2$.

The formulas were obtained from direct computations in bounded ranges and, if valid uniformly, would extend the determinant description to all the indicated hook-partition parameters.
source: Benjamin Morris and Paul P. Martin, “On semisimplicity criteria and non-semisimple representation theory for the Kadar-Yu algebras”, arXiv:2512.24535 (2025).
scope: Morris-Martin Conjecture 3.31.1 gives closed formulas for the Gram determinants of the one-cup standard modules of the Kadar-Yu algebras indexed by the hook (a+1,1) and its transpose. As printed the conjecture is false: at height a = 5 and tail length 0 the determinant has degree 174 while the printed product has degree 166. The corrected formulas are proved for both families, the ordinary hook for every a >= 2 and the transposed hook for every a >= 1, for every tail length k >= 0: in (3.3.7) the exponent of the loop variable becomes (a+3)(a+2)(a-2)/6, in (3.3.10) the missing operator is a plus, and the recurrence carries the minus sign; (3.3.8) and (3.3.9) stand as printed. Credit is for the corrected uniform theorem; the literal refutation alone would be an erratum.
limits: The link between the Lean Gram matrix and the source Gram matrix is by construction, checked by an independent audit with computations from the source definitions (all 14 worked determinants of the source reproduced), not a kernel-checked theorem. Enyang-Goodman and De Visscher-Martin are unread; no new literature search in the final revision. Determinants are normalized up to a nonzero constant, as the source allows.

title: Ilinca–Kahn conjectured bipartite matching entropy bound
record_title: Ilinca–Kahn conjectured bipartite matching entropy bound
statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph on $X\cup Y$ with $|X|=\ell$ and $|Y|=M\geq \ell$. For each $x\in X$, let $d_x$ be its degree, and define

$$
\psi(d,t)=t^{-1}\bigl[\log d!-\log \Gamma(d-t+1)\bigr],
$$

where $\Gamma$ is the usual gamma function. Let $\Phi_\ell(G)$ denote the number of matchings of size $\ell$ in $G$.

**Ilinca–Kahn conjectured matching bound.** If, for each $x\in X$, $t_x=\ell d_x/M$, then

$$
\log\Phi_\ell(G)\leq \sum_{x\in X}\psi(d_x,t_x).
$$

This proposed inequality is a precise version of an earlier entropy bound discussed in the paper. The source proposes it as a conjecture and does not provide a proof or resolution.
source: Liviu Ilinca and Jeff Kahn, “Asymptotics of the Upper Matching Conjecture”, arXiv:1205.4342 (2012).
scope: For every m >= 3 the bipartite graph K_{m,m+1} together with a disjoint edge, with parts of sizes m+1 and m+2, has (m+1)! matchings saturating the smaller part, which strictly exceeds the bound of Ilinca-Kahn Conjecture 3.1; the natural-log gap is about 0.0253 at m = 3 and increases. The proof uses tangents to the convex function log Gamma for m >= 4 and an exact integer chord certificate for m = 3; within this family m = 1, 2 satisfy the bound. The special case the authors were most confident of (all left degrees equal with integral t) is not refuted and remains open.
limits: The journal version of the source (JCTA 120, 2013) and journal versions of related papers are unread; the literature search was bounded.

title: The strict lower-bound conjecture for the robust clique covering number
record_title: The strict lower-bound conjecture for the robust clique covering number
statement: Let $G$ be an isolate-free graph. Write $\theta(G)$ for its clique covering number and $\theta_1(G)$ for the corresponding robustness parameter, so that the general lower bound is $\theta_1(G)\geq\theta(G)$. **Strict lower-bound conjecture.** The inequality is strict unless $G$ is edgeless; equivalently, equality can occur only for edgeless graphs. This conjecture asks for a characterization of the equality case in the lower bound for the robust clique covering number. Its status is not established in the supplied source.
source: Gábor Bacsó, Balázs Patkós, Zsolt Tuza and Máté Vizer, “The robust chromatic number of graphs”, arXiv:2305.01923 (2023).
scope: For every finite simple graph G, the robust clique covering number theta_1(G) (the maximum, over 1-selections in which each vertex selects one incident edge, of the clique covering number after deleting the selected edges) equals the clique covering number theta(G) if and only if G has no edges. This is Conjecture 1 of the source, proved without the isolate-free hypothesis of the MathDB record. The argument modifies the proofs of Proposition 7 and Theorem 6 of the source by an explicit 1-selection. Significance is modest: a short argument on a question the source authors left open.
limits: Close call on significance (a few-line variant of the source technique; user may overrule). The journal version of the source is unread (publisher bot challenge).

title: Line-middle graph inequality conjecture for outer-connected domination
record_title: Line-middle graph inequality conjecture for outer-connected domination
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n\ge 2$, and let $L(G)$ and $M(G)$ denote its line graph and middle graph, respectively. The **line-middle graph inequality conjecture** asserts that

$$
\gamma{\tilde{}} _{c}(L(G)) \le \gamma{\tilde{}} _{c}(M(G)).
$$

The inequality is supported by the preceding results, including strict inequality for wheels of order at least five; equality occurs for at least one connected graph of order four. A classification of graphs for which equality holds is posed separately as an open problem, while the general inequality remains open.
source: Farshad Kazemnejad, Behnaz Pahlavsay, Elisa Palezzato and Michele Torielli, “Connected and outer-connected domination number of middle graphs”, arXiv:2206.15439 (2022).
scope: Conjecture 7.6 of the source (the outer-connected domination number of the line graph is at most that of the middle graph) is false: for every h >= 2 the graph formed by two copies of K_{2h} joined by a three-edge path has outer-connected domination number 2h+2 for its middle graph and C(2h,2)+h+1 for its line graph (6 against 9 at h = 2), under both conventions for an empty complement. Lean proves explicit bounds giving the strict inequality for every h and infinitely many counterexample orders; the exact values are proved in the paper. Significance is low; this is a second result from section 7 of the same source as accepted 355217.
limits: Low significance, and a second credit from the same source section as 355217 (user may overrule). Lean proves bounds sufficient for the refutation; exact values are in the written proof only.

title: The many-rank matrix-sum equidistribution conjecture
record_title: The many-rank matrix-sum equidistribution conjecture
statement:
Let $\operatorname{Mat}^{n\times n}_q$ be the additive group of $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb F_q$. For integers $r_1,\ldots,r_k,t$ with $0\le r_i,t\le n$, let $\mathcal N^{n\times n}_q(r_1,\ldots,r_k;t)$ denote the number of $k$-tuples of matrices of respective ranks $r_1,\ldots,r_k$ whose sum is a fixed matrix of rank $t$, and let $\mathcal R^{n\times n}_q(r)$ denote the number of matrices of rank $r$. **Many-rank matrix-sum equidistribution conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$ there exists $K(\epsilon)$ such that, if $k\ge K(\epsilon)$ and $\epsilon n\le r_1,\ldots,r_k\le n$, then

$$
\mathcal N^{n\times n}_q(r_1,\ldots,r_k;t)=\operatorname{O}(1)\,\frac{\mathcal R^{n\times n}_q(r_1)\cdots\mathcal R^{n\times n}_q(r_k)}{q^{n^2}}.
$$

The source introduces this as the second of two conjectural generalizations of results in the paper; no resolution status is supplied.
source: Nick Gill, Noam Lifshitz, László Pyber and Endre Szabó, “Initiating the proof of the Liebeck–Nikolov–Shalev conjecture”, arXiv:2408.07800 (2024).
scope: For n by n matrices over a finite field with q elements: if prescribed ranks r_1, ..., r_k sum to at least 2n, then for every target matrix the number of k-tuples of matrices of those ranks with that sum is at most 32768 q^(-n^2) times the product of the sizes of the rank classes. The constant is uniform in q, n, k and the ranks. With all ranks at least epsilon n and k at least ceil(2/epsilon) this proves Conjecture 5.5 of Gill, Lifshitz, Pyber and Szabo in its upper-bound (O(1)) reading; a two-sided reading is false already over F_2 with n = 1. The source proves the case of three summands of rank at least 2n/3. Significance is modest.
limits: Modest significance (user may overrule). The conjecture is read as a one-sided O(1) upper bound; the referee showed a two-sided reading is false. Journal versions of the source are unread.

title: The edge-redundant rigidity conjecture for complete graphs in $\ell_\infty^d$
record_title: The edge-redundant rigidity conjecture for complete graphs in $\ell_\infty^d$
statement:
Let $d\geq 2$, let $n\geq 2d+2$, and let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices. A graph is **edge-redundantly rigid** in a normed space if it has a framework that is infinitesimally rigid and remains infinitesimally rigid after deleting any edge. **Edge-redundant rigidity conjecture.** For every $d\geq 2$ and every $n\geq 2d+2$, the complete graph $K_n$ is edge-redundantly rigid in $\ell_\infty^d$.

The preceding proposition rules out $K_{2d+1}$, so the conjecture asserts that the stated threshold is sufficient as well as necessary. The supplied excerpt gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
source: James Cruickshank, Sean Dewar and Derek Kitson, “Algebraic connectivity in normed spaces”, arXiv:2508.00134 (2025).
scope: The complete graph K_8 is not edge-redundantly rigid in three-dimensional l-infinity space: no well-positioned placement of K_8 remains infinitesimally rigid after the removal of every single edge. This refutes the conjecture of Cruickshank, Dewar and Kitson that K_n is edge-redundantly rigid in l-infinity^d for all n >= 2d+2, at its first open case d = 3, n = 8. The proof reduces the property to a condition on the three colour classes of the framework (every colour class meets every cut twice), derives seven forbidden four-point patterns from the geometry, and shows the resulting propositional instance unsatisfiable; the certificate (12,876 steps) is checked inside the Lean kernel by a verified checker. K_9 is edge-redundantly rigid in l-infinity^3 (proved in Lean), and so is K_n for every n >= 10 (proved in the paper only).
limits: Computer-assisted: the unsatisfiability certificate is checked by a checker proved sound in Lean and evaluated in the kernel; the generated certificate modules are reproducible from the scripts and inputs in this folder. The journal version of the source (Linear Algebra Appl. 739, 2026) is unread. The extension of the positive result to n >= 10 is proved on paper only.

title: The achromatic number bound by the harmonic index
record_title: The achromatic number bound by the harmonic index
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. The **achromatic number** $psi(G)$ is the largest number of colors in a complete proper vertex coloring, and $R'(G)$ denotes the inverse degree-based index used in the source. **The achromatic-number conjecture.**

$$
\psi(G)\leq 2R'(G).
$$

The source presents this as a conjecture motivated by the preceding bounds. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
source: Baoyindureng Wu and Clive Elphick, “Upper bounds for the achromatic and coloring numbers of a graph”, arXiv:1511.00537 (2015).
scope: For every finite simple graph G with at least one edge, every complete colouring (proper or not) uses at most 2R'(G) colours, where R'(G) is the sum over edges uv of 1/max(d(u), d(v)). Hence the achromatic number, the pseudoachromatic number and the Grundy number are all at most 2R'(G), which proves Wu-Elphick Conjecture 4.1 (and 4.2) for all graphs with an edge. The literal statement "for any graph" fails exactly at nonempty edgeless graphs, where the achromatic number is 1 and R' is 0; Lean proves this exact truth set. The source excludes isolated vertices in its neighbouring results, so the result is a proof of the intended conjecture.
limits: The literal MathDB statement includes edgeless graphs, where it fails trivially; credit is for the theorem on graphs with an edge (root judgment; user may overrule). Significance modest (review 0.35). Lin and Wang, Discrete Applied Mathematics 371 (2025) 60-64, was read only in the publisher abstract and excerpts: their main theorem excludes both colouring numbers, but the full text was not accessible.

title: Positive proportion conjecture for partitions into MSTD subsets
record_title: Positive proportion conjecture for partitions into MSTD subsets
statement: A **$k$-decomposition into MSTD subsets** is a partition of $I_r=\{1,2,\ldots,r\}$ into $k$ subsets, each having more pairwise sums than pairwise differences. **Positive proportion conjecture.** For any finite $k\ge 2$, the proportion of $k$-decompositions of $I_r$ into MSTD subsets is bounded below by a positive constant. This would extend the known positive-constant lower bound for $k=2$ and give a uniform abundance result for decompositions into any fixed finite number of MSTD subsets; the source does not establish the conjecture for general $k$.
source: Hung Viet Chu, Noah Luntzlara, Steven J. Miller and Lily Shao, “Infinite Families of Partitions into MSTD Subsets”, arXiv:1808.05460 (2019).
scope: For every fixed k >= 2 there are a constant c > 0 and a threshold R such that for all r >= R at least a proportion c of the partitions of {1, ..., r} into k nonempty classes have every class an MSTD set (more sums than differences). This proves the positive-proportion conjecture of Chu, Luntzlara, Miller and Shao; the case k = 2 is due to Asada, Manski, Miller and Suh. The new ingredient is a k-colouring of Z/2hZ, h odd, in which antipodal residues get different colours and every colour class has full modular sumset, laid periodically on both ends of the interval.
limits: Significance modest (review 0.35). Journal versions and the classical MSTD papers were not read in full; no proof for k >= 3 was found in a bounded search, and the ProbXiv record is open.

title: The Jacobi-symbol conjecture for the integers $c_p$
record_title: The Jacobi-symbol conjecture for the integers $c_p$
statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime. For $\delta\in\{0,1\}$, define

$$
D_p^{(\delta)}(w)=\left|\left(\frac{j^2-k^2}{p}\right)+\left(\frac{jk}{p}\right)w\right|_{\delta\leqslant j,k\leqslant(p-1)/2}-\left|\left(\frac{j^2-k^2}{p}\right)\right|_{\delta\leqslant j,k\leqslant(p-1)/2}.
$$

For $p\equiv1\pmod4$, let $c_p$ be the positive odd integer whose existence is asserted by the preceding theorem through $D_p^{(0)}(w)=-w((p-1)c_p/2)^2$; for $p\equiv3\pmod4$, let $c_p$ be the positive odd integer whose existence is asserted through $D_p^{(1)}(w)=w(c_p\sum_{k=1}^{(p-1)/2}(\frac{k}{p}))^2$.

**Jacobi-symbol conjecture for $c_p$.** For any odd prime $p$,

$$
\left(\frac{p}{c_p}\right)=1,
$$

where $(\frac{p}{c_p})$ is the Jacobi symbol.

The conjecture is based on numerical values of $c_p$ listed in the source. The supplied text gives no resolution or proof, so its status remains open.
source: Deyi Chen and Zhi-Wei Sun, “On determinants involving (j^2-k^2p) and (jkp)”, arXiv:2408.14401 (2024).
scope: For every odd prime p, the Jacobi symbol (p / c_p) equals 1, where c_p is the positive odd integer defined by the determinant identities of Chen and Sun (Theorem 1.1 of the source); existence and uniqueness of c_p are proved as part of the statement. This is Conjecture 1.1 of the source. Orientation matters: with c_p on top the symbol is -1 for 16 of the 80 odd primes up to 419. The proof uses a Vandermonde factorization, an integer skew-block identity for p = 1 mod 4, and a signed Pfaffian with its square identity and a character evaluation for p = 3 mod 4. Significance is low to modest (review 0.3).
limits: Low to modest significance (user may overrule). No citing papers were found; arXiv keyword search and Google Scholar could not be used, and some 2026 journal papers were read only through reference lists. Related work by Ren and Luo (arXiv:2407.04556) uses similar methods on other matrices.

title: The Catalan triangle Laurent polynomial and positivity conjecture
record_title: The Catalan triangle Laurent polynomial and positivity conjecture
statement:
Let $n_1,\ldots,n_m,n_{m+1}=n_1$ be positive integers. For an integer $j$ and non-negative integers $a,r$ with $a\leqslant n_1$, consider

$$
\frac{1}{[n_m+a]}{n_1+n_m\brack n_1-a}^{-1}\sum_{k=a}^{n_1}[2k][k]^{2r}q^{jk^2-(r+1)k}\prod_{i=1}^{m}{n_i+n_{i+1}\brack n_i+k}.
$$

**Catalan triangle Laurent polynomial and positivity conjecture.** This expression is a Laurent polynomial in $q$, and it has non-negative integer coefficients when $0\leqslant j\leqslant m$. This is presented as a stronger version of Theorem and as a generalization of a conjecture attributed to Guo and Wang; the supplied span does not state whether it has since been resolved.
source: Victor J. W. Guo and Xiuguo Lian, “Proofs of two conjectures on Catalan triangle numbers”, arXiv:1806.02685 (2018).
scope: For positive integers n_1, ..., n_m with n_{m+1} = n_1, an integer j, and nonnegative integers a, r with a <= n_1, the Guo-Lian q-Catalan-triangle expression (a quotient of a sum of products of Gaussian binomial coefficients, weighted by [2k][k]^(2r) q^(j k^2 - (r+1) k)) is a Laurent polynomial in q with integer coefficients for every integer j, and all its coefficients are nonnegative for 0 <= j <= m. This is Conjecture 6.1 of Guo and Lian, who proved integrality for 0 <= j <= m. The proof introduces a nonnegative Newton-type basis in which the signed recurrence acts positively, and uses interpolation at the roots of the denominator. The range 0 <= j <= m for nonnegativity is sharp (written proof only). MathDB 339461 is a duplicate record of the same conjecture and is credited once.
limits: MathDB 339461 is a duplicate record; submit once and reference both. The full text of Li and Wang (2026) on q-Narayana divisibility is unread (publisher blocks automated access); its abstract concerns a different conjecture. The sharpness of the range is proved on paper only.
